correctness.rationale: Prime ℓ has exponent divisors {1,ℓ}, while every prime in squarefree m has exponent one, so d_e=2, σ_e=mp(1+p^{ℓ-1}), and S_e=1+p^{ℓ-1}. Type 1 would force 1+p^{ℓ-1}|2p^{ℓ-1}; coprimality with p reduces this to divisibility by 2, impossible. Type 2 reduces exactly to 1+p^{ℓ-1}|2m. Cancelling its gcd with 2 yields M|m; since m is squarefree this is equivalent to M squarefree and the stated coprime factorization. An independent direct-definition sweep checked 5,700 small admissible triples with no discrepancy. The argument is complete for all stated parameters.

final_claim: For prime ℓ, prime p and squarefree m coprime to p, n=p^ℓm is never exponential harmonic of type 1 and is of type 2 exactly when p^{ℓ-1}+1 divides 2m; equivalently M=(p^{ℓ-1}+1)/gcd(p^{ℓ-1}+1,2) must be squarefree and m=Ms with s squarefree and gcd(s,pM)=1, with the two-prime-support case exactly q=M prime.
